title: Etale descent of fine log structures and morphisms
statement:
Let $T$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] with a jointly surjective etale covering $\{j_a:T_a\to T\}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. On each $T_a$ let $M_a$ be a log structure in the sense of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], fine in that it has etale-local charts by finitely generated integral monoids. Suppose the $M_a$ are equipped with isomorphisms on $T_a\times_TT_b$ [def-pc-fibre-product] compatible with their structure maps to the structure sheaf, restricting to identities on the diagonals and satisfying the cocycle condition on triple overlaps. Then there exists a fine log structure $M$ on $T$ with compatible identifications of its restrictions with $M_a$ inducing the datum, unique up to unique isomorphism compatible with those identifications. If every $M_a$ admits etale-local charts by fine saturated monoids, then $M$ does also.

Moreover, let $A,B$ be sheaves of commutative monoids on $T_{\mathrm{Et}}$ (their underlying presheaves of sets are sheaves, their sections are commutative monoids, and restriction maps are monoid homomorphisms), with homomorphisms $\alpha:A\to(\mathcal O_T,\cdot)$ and $\beta:B\to(\mathcal O_T,\cdot)$. Let $u_a:A|_{T_a}\to B|_{T_a}$ be homomorphisms of monoid sheaves satisfying $\beta|_{T_a}\circ u_a=\alpha|_{T_a}$ and agreeing on every double overlap. Here restriction is to the localized small etale site over $T_a$, with its structure sheaf $\mathcal O_{T_a}$. Then there is a unique homomorphism $u:A\to B$ with $\beta\circ u=\alpha$ restricting to every $u_a$. The sheaves $A$ and $B$ may be arbitrary; in particular this assertion applies to inverse-image monoid sheaves equipped with the composite structure map to $\mathcal O_T$.

source.place: Expose VIII, §3.3.8 final sentence, printed pp. 107--108 (descent from strict etale charts); Expose VI, §1.1--1.4 for fine/fs log structures. The arbitrary-monoid-sheaf morphism clause is the ordinary sheaf gluing condition applied sectionwise; it does not require the source to be a log structure.

proof.text: Use the small representatives of the sites in [def-weil-size-convention], in a universe also containing the covering index set and the section sets and products used in descent. Put $\mathcal C=T_{\mathrm{Et}}$ and take its terminal object $T\to T$. The given family covers that object, and fibre products exist in $\mathcal C$, by [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open], $\mathcal C/T_a$ is the small etale site of $T_a$, and likewise on all overlaps. Thus the given $M_a$ and their transitions are sheaves and maps on the slice sites required for descent. Under these equivalences the structure sheaves agree: on an object $W\to T_a$ both assign $\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$, with the same restrictions. Relocalization in [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] gives the same identifications on repeated slices; the slice over the terminal object is $\mathcal C$ itself.

source.place: Section 00XZ, section-localize; Definition 00Y0, definition-localize; Lemma 03EH, lemma-relocalize; specialization to the small etale sites

proof.text: Forget the monoid operations for the moment. Apply the existence clause of [lem-pe-set-sheaf-cover-descent] to the underlying set sheaves of $M_a$ and their given transition isomorphisms $\phi_{ab}$. The assumed cocycle is exactly its cocycle, including repeated indices. Obtain a sheaf of sets $M$ and isomorphisms $e_a:M|_{T_a}\xrightarrow{\sim}M_a$ with $e_b=\phi_{ab}e_a$ on every double overlap. These identifications induce the specified descent datum, rather than only isomorphic unlabelled local objects.

source.place: Tag 04TR, lemma-glue-sheaves, with the gluing datum immediately preceding it

proof.text: For $W\to T$ etale put $W_a=W\times_TT_a$. For $s,t\in M(W)$, transport their restrictions by $e_a$, multiply in $M_a(W_a)$, and transport back. The resulting sections of $M(W_a)$ agree on double overlaps because $\phi_{ab}$ is a monoid homomorphism. The equalizer condition of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets] gives a unique product in $M(W)$; glue the local identity sections in the same way. These operations commute with restriction, since each proposed restriction is the unique section with the indicated local values. Associativity, commutativity and both identity laws hold after restriction to every $W_a$, hence hold in $M(W)$ by the injective part of the same equalizer condition. Thus $M$ is a sheaf of commutative monoids and each $e_a$ is a monoid isomorphism. The local maps $\alpha_a e_a:M|_{T_a}\to\mathcal O_T|_{T_a}$ agree on overlaps by the assumed compatibility of structure maps. The morphism clause of [lem-pe-set-sheaf-cover-descent] glues them to $\alpha:M\to\mathcal O_T$. Its multiplication and identity equations hold locally, so the same separatedness argument proves that $\alpha$ is a monoid homomorphism.

source.place: Tag 04TQ, lemma-glue-maps; monoid operations and their equations obtained sectionwise from the sheaf equalizer condition

proof.text: Check the log condition of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] directly. For an etale object $W$ and $v\in\mathcal O_T(W)^\times$, its restriction to $W_a$ has a unique preimage $m_a\in M(W_a)$ under $\alpha$, since $(M_a,\alpha_a)$ is a log structure and $e_a$ is a monoid isomorphism. On every double overlap the two preimages agree by that same local uniqueness. The sheaf condition [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets] glues them to $m\in M(W)$, and separatedness gives $\alpha(m)=v$. If two such preimages existed, their restrictions would be equal on all $W_a$, so they would be equal. Consequently the natural map $\alpha^{-1}(\mathcal O_T^\times)\to\mathcal O_T^\times$ is bijective on every object and therefore is an isomorphism of monoid sheaves. This makes $(M,\alpha)$ a log structure.

source.place: Expose VI, 1.1, printed p. 69; verification of the defining log condition under the sheaf gluing used in Expose VIII, 3.3.8

proof.text: For each $a$ choose an etale covering $\{V_{a\lambda}\to T_a\}$ on which $M_a$ has its given fine charts. Composite coverings cover in the site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], so the $V_{a\lambda}\to T$ form an etale covering. On each member transport its chart $P_{a\lambda}\to M_a|_{V_{a\lambda}}$ through $e_a^{-1}$. This is a chart for $M$: its composite to the structure sheaf is unchanged and its chart map is followed by an isomorphism of monoid sheaves. In particular the stalkwise pushout map in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] is the old chart isomorphism followed by the stalk of $e_a^{-1}$. Each $P_{a\lambda}$ is still finitely generated and integral. Thus $M$ is fine. If the local charts were fine saturated, exactly the same charts remain saturated, so $M$ is fs. No single global chart, or Zariski-local chart, is asserted.

source.place: Expose VI, 1.1, printed p. 69; Expose VIII, Remark 3.3.4(ii) and 3.3.8, printed p. 107

proof.text: For the moreover clause apply the morphism clause of [lem-pe-set-sheaf-cover-descent] to the underlying set sheaves of $A,B$ and the maps $u_a$. It gives a unique set-sheaf map $u:A\to B$. For $s,t\in A(W)$ the sections $u(st)$ and $u(s)u(t)$ restrict to equal sections on $W_a$, by the homomorphism property of $u_a$; hence they are equal by [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets]. The same argument gives $u(1)=1$ and $\beta u=\alpha$. Thus $u$ is the required monoid-sheaf map over the structure sheaf, and uniqueness already follows from uniqueness as a set-sheaf map. This argument assumes only the stated sheaf and monoid axioms of $A,B$, so it also applies when the source is an inverse-image monoid sheaf with the specified composite structure map; no log axiom for the source is used.

source.place: Tag 04TQ, lemma-glue-maps, on the slice over the terminal object; the monoid and structure-map equations checked sectionwise

proof.text: Finally let $(N,\gamma)$ be another fine log structure with identifications $f_a:N|_{T_a}\xrightarrow{\sim}M_a$ inducing this datum. The monoid-sheaf maps $f_a^{-1}e_a:M|_{T_a}\to N|_{T_a}$ agree on double overlaps and commute with the structure maps. By the moreover argument just proved (using the morphism clause of [lem-pe-set-sheaf-cover-descent]) they glue uniquely to a monoid-sheaf map $h:M\to N$ over $\mathcal O_T$. Glue the inverses $e_a^{-1}f_a$ in the same way. Both composites restrict to identity maps; uniqueness in that same morphism clause makes both composites identities. Hence $h$ is an isomorphism, and every isomorphism compatible with the identifications has precisely these local maps, so equals $h$. This proves uniqueness in the asserted, identification-preserving sense.

source.place: Tag 04TQ, lemma-glue-maps; uniqueness of the gluing and gluing of the inverse maps

split_report.summary: Expanded the omitted fine-log-structure descent argument through existing effective descent for set sheaves. Constructed monoid operations and the structure map, verified the log-unit condition sectionwise, retained the actual local charts to prove fine/fs locality, and proved the arbitrary-monoid morphism clause and identification-preserving uniqueness. No new nodes; no statement change.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the strict-etale descent input in Expose VIII 3.3.8 reached from lem-trf-local-term-locality through the recorded ancestry; generic sheaf descent is a tool, not a replacement of the contracting-correspondence route.

tool_uses.why: Generic effective descent and unique morphism gluing for set sheaves, Stacks 04TR/04TQ; this unit has no such sheaf-theoretic tool.
Generic equivalence of a localized small etale site with the etale site of its object; needed to apply the slice-site descent theorem to the supplied log structures.

lean.statement: theorem fineLogStructure_etale_descent {T : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian T] {ι : Type v} (U : ι → T.Etale) (hcover : ∀ x : T, ∃ (a : ι) (y : (U a).left), (U a).hom y = x) : (∀ D : FineLogEtaleDescentDatum U, ∃ (M : EtaleLogStructure T) (_hM : M.IsFine) (e : D.Gluing M), ((∀ a : ι, (D.localLog a).IsFineSaturated) → M.IsFineSaturated) ∧ ∀ (N : EtaleLogStructure T) (_hN : N.IsFine) (f : D.Gluing N), ∃! h : EtalePrelogStructure.Iso M.toEtalePrelogStructure N.toEtalePrelogStructure, ∀ (a : ι) (V : T.Etale) (g : V ⟶ U a) (s : M.monoidSheaf.obj.obj (op V)), f.component a V g (h.iso.hom.app (op V) s) = e.component a V g s) ∧ (∀ (A B : EtalePrelogStructure T) (localHom : ∀ a : ι, A.LocalHom B (U a)), (∀ (a b : ι) (V : T.Etale) (f : V ⟶ U a) (g : V ⟶ U b), (localHom a).hom.app (op (Over.mk f)) = (localHom b).hom.app (op (Over.mk g))) → ∃! h : A.Hom B, ∀ (a : ι) (V : T.Etale) (f : V ⟶ U a), h.hom.app (op V) = (localHom a).hom.app (op (Over.mk f)))
